account:
Today I have followed my mayoral appointments: the morning office business, a ten o'clock mill inspection, lunch at home, and council letters at thirteen. I am now at the neighbour's east-dock cottage for three o'clock tea, with an office review due at sixteen thirty. No new council correspondence had reached the secretary today.

The unusual thing is repeated, vague talk of a bridge or port change at the bakery. Several townspeople have repeated much the same report, naming the baker and sometimes the neighbour. One report said the baker carried a sack of bread. I have not witnessed a change to any crossing or established what the reports mean. It could concern transport or deliveries, but that is only a possibility. I asked the neighbour for clarification and about Freight's concerns, without receiving a substantive answer yet. I should not treat these rumours as confirmed infrastructure news.

At the mill stall I personally saw 128 hay bales. I did not establish storage conditions, delivery arrangements, or the keeper's account, so the inspection leaves those matters unresolved.

Builder reports that the inn door worked normally and that he supplied and fitted an authorized lantern clear of the passage for four emeralds, paid in full. He expressly did not verify sleeping arrangements or certify guest readiness. He also reports no visible defect at the east ferry landing, but says this was not a comprehensive structural inspection. These are Builder's reports, not findings I personally checked. The secretary is preparing a written record for the afternoon review; I asked that its limitations be explicit. The earlier agreed inspection fee was two emeralds, distinct from the one emerald supplied for an office writing book. I see ordinary maintenance and recordkeeping underway, but do not yet know whether the bakery rumours relate to any of it.
